thread:
alex: Deploy-bot just flagged a p99 latency spike on canary (v3.9.0). Auto-revert did NOT kick. Anyone on call?

deploy-bot: ALERT v3.9.0-canary: p99 > 800ms for 5m. Auto-revert threshold=1000ms. No auto action taken. Logs: ```canary/2025-11-02T17:04:21Z p99=812ms\ncanary/2025-11-02T17:05:21Z p99=790ms```

alex: Ok thanks. looks like it hovered under auto threshold but still worrying. @sasha can you check traces and whether rollout traffic slice is stuck?

sasha: On it, pulling traces now. Quick note: traffic slice still at 20% for canary. No errors in app logs but we see a spike in inference queue depth on one host. Might be KV cache warm-up.

jamie: If it's cache warm-up, we should avoid a full rollback — maybe pin the canary bucket to v3.8.7 for dedicated routes and throttle traffic back to 0% for canary while we investigate. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

maria: Agree. Ops prefers manual hold + comms instead of noisy auto-revert for cache artifacts. We should notify customers on dedicated pools if we change routing.

ops-oncall: I'll hold traffic at the LB level. Command: ```deployctl traffic set canary 0% --id=canary-slice-42``` will drain gradually. Can run now if release owners approve.

alex: Approve. jamie, can you pin the release for dedicated tiers and prepare release note snippet for rollback/handoff? We need to be explicit: this is a manual hold due to KV cache warm-up, not a functional regression.

jamie: On it. Pinning dedicated routing to v3.8.7: ```releasectl pin --pool=dedicated-eu --version=3.8.7 --reason="temporary pin due to canary p99 spike"```

jamie: Draft release note for comms: "We paused canary for v3.9.0 due to transient inference queueing during KV cache warm-up. No user-facing errors observed. Engineers are investigating; canary will resume after warm-up verification. Contact support if you see persistent latency." Will post to #customer-notify after ops confirms traffic hold.

sasha: Traces show a single host with abnormal queueing — recreating container shows cache rebuild latency. Rolling a restart on that host is low-risk. Recommend restart before resuming traffic.

maria: +1 to restart and gradual ramp. Also set a watch: if p99 > 1000ms for 2 consecutive 5m windows, we escalate to full rollback. Let's document that in the thread.

alex: Agreed. Escalation criteria: auto-revert threshold remains 1000ms, but manual policy: if p99 > 1000ms for 10m OR error-rate > 1.5% for 5m then initiate rollback to 3.8.7 and notify customers.

deploy-bot: ACK policy update. Will notify when thresholds breached.

ops-oncall: Traffic hold applied. Command result: `OK - canary traffic set to 0% (drain in progress)`. Rolling restart on suspect host now.

jamie: Restart done, monitoring. p99 back to ~420ms across canary slice. Ramping to 5% over 10m.

maria: I'll prep a short broadcast for customers on the dedicated plan explaining the temporary pause and the mitigation steps. Link to support article + contact.

alex: Thanks all. Leaving this thread as the single source of truth for the decision: manual hold -> pin dedicated -> restart -> gradual ramp. If policy triggers rollback, ops to run `releasectl rollback --version=3.8.7 --reason=auto-or-manual-trigger` and we notify customers.

jamie: Noted. I'll update the internal release notes and mark postmortem owners if this reappears.

sasha: Monitoring looks stable for now. Will ping if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
